title: VNX 0.1 — Viatrail Network eXchange
description: Structural schema for a VNX 0.1 document. READ schema/README.md before trusting a green result: a JSON Schema can check shape, and several of this format's load-bearing rules are not about shape. It is deliberately permissive about unknown keys, because spec §6.2 makes an unknown key a reader DIAGNOSTIC and keeps the item — a schema that refused them would disagree with every conforming reader.

vnx.description: The specification version, MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH. All three components are required: the two-component spelling is refused, not coerced. Whether a reader can READ this version is reader-relative and outside a schema's reach. THIS FILE IS NAMED FOR THE MINOR SERIES and covers every patch of it, because a patch bump is additive by definition (spec §2.1); a new minor gets a new schema file.

rulesets.description: Carried VERBATIM and never interpreted (spec §3.7). The subsystem is being redesigned; a 0.1 reader preserves the block so a later one can read it, and validates nothing inside it. So this schema does not either.

timestamp.description: ISO 8601, UTC, Z suffix, optional fractional seconds — and nothing else (spec §4.3). Pinning one grammar is cheaper than five implementations each discovering their platform's date parser the hard way.

identifier.description: Container-scoped and document-local. A route's node-1 and a network's node-1 are DIFFERENT nodes; a reader that builds one global map merges them. That rule is about scope, not shape, so nothing here can enforce it.

position.description: Fixed positional channels: [lon, lat, ele, time_ms]. From index 2, null means ABSENT — a first-class state, not a zero. Channels beyond index 3 are ignored rather than refused, so a future fifth channel is additive rather than a flag day. ⚠ Nothing here can catch a lon/lat transposition: both orderings are numbers, both are in range, and the point lands 8000 km away with this schema still green. See testdata/corpus/accept/lonlat-transposition.vnx.

record.description: One element of a `data` bag (spec §5). Apart from @type the body is OPAQUE and must stay so: an unknown type is inert on any host, and its fields survive read-modify-write at value level. A schema that constrained the body would break exactly the extensibility the bag exists for.

ring.description: ONE closed ring — this format cannot express holes. `minItems: 4` is three distinct positions plus the closing repeat. That the last position actually REPEATS the first is a relationship between two values, which JSON Schema cannot state; the reader checks it. Nested rings ARE caught here, because a ring element must be a position and a position's first element must be a number.

style.description: A style object is OPAQUE (SPEC 3.10): a reader carries every key through a read-modify-write and reports none of them as unrecognised, so this definition constrains almost nothing. `importance` is the one exception, because it is the one style value SPEC 3.6 gives a normative range. Nothing else here is typed ON PURPOSE, not by omission: SPEC 3.6 states that `icon-size` has no stated range and that `"icon-size": "large"` therefore passes unremarked, so a schema typing it as an integer would refuse a document every conforming reader accepts. One definition rather than three because the reference implementation's style is a plain map — a point, an area and a chain do not carry different shapes.

importance.description: SPEC 3.6: an integer from 1 to 5, normatively. A value outside the range is an unusable value in an optional field (SPEC 6.2).

segment.description: A segment boundary is a PAUSE, not chunking. The gap between two segments is not geometry and not walking — a reader that joins them draws a line nobody walked and counts time nobody spent moving.

anonymousArc.description: An arc inside a top-level route. It has NO id and no from/to: a route owns its geometry outright and shares it with nothing, which is the whole difference between a route and a chain over a network.

route.description: Arc boundaries are MEANING, not chunking: they are where the user changed how the line was made. A reader that concatenates the pip lists into one polyline loses that, and nothing errors.

namedArc.description: An arc inside a network, referenced by key. Two chains crossing the same trail name the SAME arc — that sharing is the meaning of the whole format, and it is a reference relationship no schema can verify.

endpoint.description: Either a node key or an inline position ON the named arc — a chain-private handle for a mid-arc start, end or turnaround. Which of the two it is, whether the node exists, and whether the position lies anywhere near the arc are all beyond a schema.

nodes.description: ⚠ Two entries with the SAME key resolve last-wins in every mainstream parser, before this schema ever runs, so a node vanishes and nothing anywhere can say so (spec §6.4). A documented cannot-detect.
